answer_to_lane_question.does_anyone_charge_for_mcp_serving: YES, three proven shapes: (1) metered RPC hosting: Smithery free 50K RPC/mo then $10/mo with $0.10 per 1K RPC overage; (2) subscription-bundled metering: Zapier MCP included in every Zapier plan, each tool call consumes 2 tasks from the plan quota; (3) metered tool-call APIs behind MCP: Composio 100,000 free tool calls/mo, pay for more, no per-seat pricing. Glama sells registry+hosting+gateway as one commercial product but its pricing page is behind a sign-up wall (reported as not verified, not guessed).
answer_to_lane_question.are_there_paid_registries: The official registry (modelcontextprotocol/registry) is free, community-driven, no payment language in its README (preview 2025-09-08, API freeze v0.1 2025-10-24). Commercial registry+hosting hybrids exist (Glama; search-level leads: XPack, Sentinel, Moesif billing infra). No first-hand evidence found of a registry charging for LISTING alone.
answer_to_lane_question.are_token_or_crypto_rails_bolted_to_mcp: YES: x402 (Coinbase origin, now x402 Foundation with Cloudflare) ships an official MCP guide (docs/guides/mcp-server-with-x402) and an MCP example server (examples/typescript/servers/mcp) in the canonical repo; Apify (blog 2026-06-30) put 20,000+ Actors on USDC-on-Base x402 payments, states MCP clients can read payment requirements from tool metadata and auto-pay, and shipped x402 support in its mcpc MCP client. Cloudflare pay-per-crawl (2025-07-01) is the fiat twin at the content layer: HTTP 402 + crawler-price header, with Cloudflare as Merchant of Record (a middleman).
answer_to_lane_question.market_adoption_reality: Contested and unverified either way: one search digest claims x402 volume collapsed ~77% from a $5.15M Nov-2025 peak to $1.19M by May 2026 (cryptorank.io); a follow-up search could not confirm it and surfaced a counter-claim of 50M+ transactions / $50M+ cumulative volume (dev.to, Feb 2026). Both recorded as search-level only. The verified core remains: dominant rails in production MCP are still API keys, Stripe-style credits, and platform quotas (web2 middlemen).

comparison_to_law_card.what_the_market_confirms: The law's core sentence is directionally confirmed: capability serving (MCP endpoints) is becoming a priced product, and the newest rail (x402) writes the law's own falsifier into its principles - 'Open standard: ... It will never force reliance on a single party' and 'Trust minimizing: all payment schemes must not allow for the facilitator or resource server to move funds, other than in accordance with client intentions' (coinbase/x402 README, fetched).
comparison_to_law_card.where_the_market_is_behind_the_law: Every commercial MCP surface that charges today still inserts a trusted party the law would name: Smithery (host + managed OAuth + credit wallet), Zapier (platform quota unit + auth 'managed by Zapier'), Composio (platform meter), Glama ('a gateway you control' sold as product), Cloudflare pay-per-crawl (Merchant of Record aggregating and distributing). x402 ships a self-facilitation example server (examples/typescript/servers/self-facilitation, GitHub API listing) - the middleman-free configuration exists in the reference repo but is not the commercial default.
comparison_to_law_card.law_card_falsifier_applied_to_market: Per the card's falsifier discipline, the named trusted parties per shipped rail: Smithery credit wallet + host; Zapier task-quota meter + auth vault; Composio meter; Glama gateway; Cloudflare MoR; x402 default facilitator (hedged by the trust-minimizing principle, eliminable via self-facilitation). The estate card's own residue (deployer key, toncenter indexer) is the same class of named party - the card is already honest by its own standard.
comparison_to_law_card.verdict: Law holds. No revision needed. One sharpening adopted (see decision_changed).
